items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: There was a known after-hours place called the Footlight Club, which was run by a fellow called Freddie Woods.

ctx.x: In the meantime, in 1938, I was made to join the union for some job that I was on -- I don't remember which one. But even after I joined the union, I hadn't considered myself a professional musician. But when after I'd worked with Tommy Miles' band and began to meet all these professionals, guys that would come to the theatre and all of that, then I decided I'd just as soon do this as anything else, and what else did I want to do -- I couldn't think of anything else.

In the meantime, there were a couple of clubs down at Seventh and T Streets, Northwest, where... I would go in there after I got off work... There was a known after-hours place called the Footlight Club, which was run by a fellow called Freddie Woods. And that was where all the musicians and anybody who came in town used to congregate.
